blocks.title: Risk Register, Tolerance, and Appetite exam shortcuts
items: Need one place to track all risks → RISK REGISTER
The register is the authoritative risk list.
Example: It records owner, likelihood, impact, and treatment.
Metric warns that risk is increasing → KRI
Example: Rapidly rising failed backups signal recovery risk.
Question asks who is accountable → RISK OWNER
Every important risk should have an owner.
Example: The application owner manages application-availability risk.
Metric crosses a point that requires action → RISK THRESHOLD
Example: More than 2 hours of downtime triggers executive escalation.
Overall willingness to take risk → RISK APPETITE
Example: A startup may have expansionary appetite.
Specific acceptable amount around an objective → RISK TOLERANCE
Example: Maximum acceptable service outage is 30 minutes.
blocks.example: Watch for formula clues, recovery-time wording, and the difference between broad risk appetite and specific risk tolerance.

questions.q: An organization keeps one central record containing each risk, its owner, likelihood, impact, status, and treatment. What is this?
questions.explanation: A risk register is the central record used to track identified risks.

questions.q: The percentage of failed backups rises sharply and is used as an early warning that recovery risk is increasing. What is this metric?
questions.explanation: A Key Risk Indicator signals changing or increasing risk exposure.

questions.q: A specific manager is accountable for monitoring and managing the risk of a critical application outage. What role is this?
questions.explanation: A risk owner is accountable for managing a specific risk.

questions.q: A policy requires executive escalation when service downtime exceeds two hours. What is the two-hour value?
questions.explanation: A risk threshold is a trigger point that requires action or escalation.

questions.q: A startup is willing to accept relatively high risk to pursue rapid growth. Which risk appetite best fits?
questions.explanation: Expansionary appetite reflects greater willingness to accept risk for growth or opportunity.

questions.q: A safety-critical organization strongly prefers low risk even if that slows growth. Which appetite best fits?
questions.explanation: A conservative appetite favors lower risk and stronger safeguards.

questions.q: An organization broadly defines itself as willing to take moderate risk, but specifies that a critical service may be unavailable for no more than 30 minutes. The 30-minute limit is an example of what?
questions.explanation: Risk tolerance is the specific acceptable variation around an objective; appetite is the broader strategic willingness to take risk.
